newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby wheat ends up on oversold signals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby wheat ends up on oversold signals.

text.p: Signals the wheat market was short-term oversold after the sharp break Thursday boosted nearby contracts to a higher close, traders said.
Skepticism about rumors of an Australian sale of wheat to Egypt also may have contributed to the gains but contract lows were set in early dealings, they said.
"Wheat just got overextended (during Thursday's drop) and some of the stories out there apparently weren't true," Cermak said, referring to the gains in December in late dealings.
Wheat fell Thursday on bearish news from the EU.

The EU hiked export subsidies for wheat and there was significant amounts of unwinding of CBOT/KCBT and CBOT/MGE spreads plus broad based fund and commercial selling during Thursday's session, the traders said.
Friday the market attempted to consolidate despite a rumor Egypt was buying 1.5 million tonnes of wheat from Australia for shipment throughout next year, they said.
Gains in wheat were limited by slow exports as evidenced by the paltry number seen Thursday in USDA's sales data, traders said.
Wheat closed 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with December up 5-3/4 at $3.89-3/4.
The new contract low for March is $3.78, down from the previous low of $3.79 set Thursday.
Technical traders said the key moving averages (MA) indicate wheat remains in a downtrend.

Chartists pointed to support in the December at $3.78 and resistance at $3.94. The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 27. Traders generally consider an RSI of 20 or less as very oversold.
Key players included Lehman Bros with two million bushels purchased in the December and O'Connor and Co bought one million December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, down from 20,746 Thursday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, LIT America bought 450 December $4.40 calls at 1/2 cent, Continental Grain bought 700 March $3.90 puts and sold 700 March $4.20 puts at 22 to 22-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000 contracts, down from 8,638 Thursday.
